newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA blamed for Seville blast, more bombs reported.
newsitem.headline: ETA blamed for Seville blast, more bombs reported.

text.p: A small bomb exploded on Tuesday injuring a construction worker in the southern Spanish city of Seville in what officials called an attack by ETA Basque separatist rebels.
"Everything points to it being an action of the ETA band of assassins," Seville's Mayor Soledad Becerril told journalists.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has often used small bombs in its 29-year independence drive in which it has killed some 800 people.
Police said nine other devices exploded last Friday at electricity towers belonging to Sevillana de Electricidad in Seville. News of the other bombs was not released until Tuesday.
The bomb at the construction site went off at 2.15 p.m. (1215 GMT) slightly injuring a 46-year-old worker who was sent to hospital.

The 200 workers at the site, near Seville's Santa Justa railway station and 50 metres (yards) from a day care centre, had been evacuated three times because of bomb threats on Friday, Monday and earlier on Tuesday.
In each instance, work restarted at the building site after police sniffer dogs searched the area.

A caller speaking in the name of ETA said on Friday that bombs had been planted at the construction site and at a railway bridge of the high speed AVE train, which leaves from Santa Justa, officials said.

In a separate incident on Tuesday, a home-made bomb exploded at a house in the Basque city of Vitoria but no one was hurt. The attack was apparently aimed at the ruling Popular Party's leader in the Basque region, whose parents live in the house.
